Timestep selection during training:
• For each training example, t is sampled uniformly from {1, . . . , T} (not sequentially). Thanks to
the kernel, xt
is created in one step.
• This trains one network on all noise levels simultaneously, which is efficient and unbiased (each
term of the loss is a random sample of the full sum over t).
• The network receives t (as a sinusoidal embedding) so it knows the noise level; small t teaches
fine detail removal, large t teaches global structure.
• Importance sampling or loss weighting over t (e.g. by SNR) can further reduce variance and
improve results.

The U-Net is a symmetric encoder–decoder convolutional network whose output has the same size
as its input. In DDPM it maps (xt

Major components and their functions:
1. Encoder (contracting path): Repeated [ResBlock(s) → downsample (stride-2 conv or pool￾ing)]. Spatial size halves and channels increase at each level. It extracts increasingly abstract,
larger-context features (edges → textures → object parts).
2. Bottleneck: Lowest resolution, highest channel count. Usually ResBlocks plus self-attention,
giving a global view of the whole image so that the network understands overall structure and
the global noise pattern.
3. Decoder (expanding path): Repeated [upsample (nearest/transposed conv) → concatenate
skip → ResBlock(s)]. Restores spatial resolution back to the input size.
4. Skip connections: Concatenate encoder feature maps with decoder feature maps at the same
resolution, passing fine spatial detail directly across.
5. Residual blocks: GroupNorm → SiLU → Conv → (add time embedding) → GroupNorm →
SiLU → Conv, with output y = x + F(x).
6. Attention layers: Self-attention at low resolutions (e.g. 16 × 16, 8 × 8) for long-range depen￾dencies; cross-attention for text conditioning (Q10).
7. Timestep embedding: Sinusoidal encoding of t → MLP → added (or used as scale/shift) in
every ResBlock, so one network handles all noise levels.
8. Output layer: GroupNorm → SiLU → 3 × 3 conv to 3 channels, giving the predicted noise
with the same shape as the image.
